


I do a lot of projects for fun, but not all of them succeed enough to put on the blog. Here's a list of some recent ones that didn't pan out, despite several weeks of effort for each one.


**ggufr**: An LLM inferencer in base R, mainly to learn the general structure to work towards making one on something sillier like an arduino nano. I have the whole structure running, but there's a bug somewhere. Debugging will require learning pytorch— that's a project for another time.

**awkme**: A oneliner awk script (my favorite language) intended to locate (multilaterate, like GPS) the user using machine learning with the signal strength of nearby wifi networks. Could use more testing, but appears to be a harder ML problem than expected— such that solving likely isn't feasible with a small awk script.

**tunnelvision**: A method for upscaling drone footage under certain circumstances by stacking frames as the drone travels forward. Mostly for image processing practice, but I came up with a neat technique for stacking— it just didn't end up working. One of this big villains of this project was moustache distortion, funnily enough...
